Visual identity system
01 / Moodboard

A visual territory shaped by the road, silence and an obsession with detail.

02 / Storytelling

The journey as proof. Gear as a language.

The story does not rely on loud performance claims. It relies on preparation, precision, endurance and the ability to go far with less.

Every visual should feel like departure is imminent. A loaded bike. An open map. Low light. A technical accessory. A focused body.

01

Autonomy

Leave, manage, repair, keep moving.

02

Precision

Every object has a function. Nothing is decorative.

03

Silence

The art direction avoids aggression. It lets the landscapes breathe.

04

Texture

Dust, textile, metal, skin, glass, road.

03 / Photography

Technical macro, warm light, physical sensation.

The glasses become a narrative screen. Reflections carry the landscape. Close-ups create a premium tension between sport, product and road imagination.

Target contrast: natural skin, harsh light, orange glass, black details, technical materials.

04 / Palette

Desaturated nature. Burnt accent. Carbon base.

The palette should remain mineral and functional. Orange accents inject energy. Carbon black gives the system its premium status. Sand and olive tones anchor the outdoor universe.

05 / Composition

Between radical order and functional disorder.

The graphic system alternates between two tensions: highly organized flatlays and near-excessive gear accumulation. This contrast gives the brand a strong personality.

Use sharp grids, generous margins, editorial layering, cut-out objects and short technical captions.

06 / Social media system

A social grid designed like a premium road journal.

The feed alternates between immersion, product details, roads, gear and moments of pause. Every post should work on its own while building a coherent world.

Final statement

The road is the identity.

An art direction for a bikepacking brand that sells more than a product: a way to leave, to equip yourself and to inhabit the road.
